# Architectural decisions

Project-wide decisions for MDÂ². The app is a Vite React web app in `app/`; `desktop/` is a separate Electron host that can load the website and expose local capabilities through preload bridges.

## File naming

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Code files use lowercase snake_case names. | All code files in `app/src/` and `desktop/` use lowercase words separated by underscores, for example `github_auth_service.ts`, `project_workspace.tsx`, and `local_git_service.js`. Test files keep the same base name with `.test` before the extension, for example `github_auth_service.test.ts`. Exported symbols keep normal TypeScript/JavaScript casing such as `GithubAuthService`, `ProjectWorkspace`, and `useGithubAuth`. | A single file naming convention avoids mixed PascalCase, camelCase, and hyphenated filenames, and keeps imports predictable across Windows and case-sensitive environments. |

## Services and state

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Global singleton services own domain state and logic. | Each domain is a class in `src/services/**`, instantiated once at module level and exported, for example `export const indexesService = new IndexesService()`. React components do not own domain state. | Keeps business logic out of components, testable without a DOM, and shared across windows/views without Redux, Zustand, or Context stores. |
| Service location follows usage scope. | If a service is specific to one UI element and used only there, place it beside that component. Generic or shared services, such as logging, database access, config, storage, or cross-screen domain logic, belong in `src/services/`. | Keeps component-owned behavior local while preserving `src/services/` for reusable application services. |
| Consumers use direct imports or the service injector. | Direct import when no import cycle exists; use `src/services/service_injector.js` when a cycle would occur. Every global singleton service registers itself in its constructor with `inj.register('myService', this)`. | The service graph is dense; the injector is a bare global registry that defers resolution to call time. |
| Services have a two-phase lifecycle. | Constructors only register and set unloaded state such as `null`. Config-dependent or service-dependent work runs in `init()`, `start()`, app bootstrap (`App.jsx`), or a `loaded` lifecycle event. `configService.config` is private; callers use `get`, `set`, and `clear`. | Module evaluation order is not guaranteed, so `configService` is not usable at import time. Reading config in a constructor is a bug. |

## Card state

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The application has one `Card` domain type. | Do not create separate canonical, project, snapshot, or editor card types. The card-owning service holds the loaded cards and exposes focused operations that change only the requested field. React snapshots and editor drafts are read values; they must never replace or merge a complete card. Parser bookkeeping may remain private persistence metadata, but it is not another card model. | One card concept gives state a clear owner and prevents stale copies from overwriting newer worktree, activity, ordering, policy, or body values. |
| Card UI subscribes at field level. | A component subscribes only to the primitive or stable reference it renders, using granular `EventTarget` events and `useSyncExternalStore`. Do not clone or stringify a complete card to detect a field change. Group fields only in a deliberately small, stable projection when they are always rendered together. | A one-field change allocates and rerenders only what consumes that field, keeping memory use bounded and the UI responsive. |
| Cards are serialized only at persistence boundaries. | Mutate the owned `Card` through a focused operation, then serialize its current state when the persistence batch flushes. Editor changes update only the edited field. Activity linking updates only activity references. External file changes are parsed and applied deliberately without replacing dirty local state. | Persistence remains deterministic while concurrent saves and external updates cannot discard unrelated newer values. |


## Events and React integration

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Services notify observers through their own `EventTarget`. | Services expose an `EventTarget` and dispatch named `CustomEvent` domain events such as `activeIndex`, `added`, `deleted`, or `changedBox`. Observers subscribe with `addEventListener` and unsubscribe with `removeEventListener` on the owning service. | Decouples producers from consumers without depending on Node `EventEmitter`, which is not available in the browser-first React app. |
| Custom hooks bridge service events to functional components. | Hooks in `src/components/hooks/`, such as `useActiveIndex` and `useProjectConfig`, seed `useState` from a service property, subscribe in `useEffect`, unsubscribe in cleanup, and return the value. Prefer hook + service over prop chains. | Components stay declarative and avoid direct event plumbing. |
| Components subscribe at the smallest rendering boundary. | Root and layout components compose UI regions and pass structural inputs. Components that render changing application data subscribe through hooks themselves. Do not hoist changing data into ancestors only to pass it downward. | Limits rerenders to affected UI, protects transient state such as open popups, and avoids broad prop chains. |
| Components use the app theme service path. | `App` owns theme mode through `useThemeMode()`, builds the MUI theme with `createAppTheme(mode)`, and provides it through `ThemeProvider`. Components read theme values with MUI APIs such as `useTheme`, `useMediaQuery`, and `sx`; only controls that change the palette mode receive `mode` and `onToggleTheme`. | Theme state, persistence, and palette construction stay centralized while components remain presentation-focused. |

The new pin-state architecture is implemented, and conversations no longer contain `pinned`. Seven problems remain.

1. **Critical — Card conversations are still missing from project-wide loading.**  
   [AgentIntegration](C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2_workers/dev1/app/src/services/agents/agent_integration.ts:379) expects `listAgentConversationReferences()` to include card conversations. Its desktop implementation only reads project activity at [activity_files.js](C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2_workers/dev1/desktop/src/actions/activity/activity_files.js:484). The status popup will miss most card-owned pins.  
   **Fix:** Combine project references with every current card’s `agentLogReferences`, loading card activity through `loadActivityConversations()`. The current test incorrectly mocks the reference API as returning both kinds.

2. **High — Concurrent settings save can overwrite a confirmed pin change.**  
   Pin updates read and merge the latest disk config at [project_files.js](C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2_workers/dev1/desktop/src/project/project_files.js:373). Normal config saving writes the complete renderer snapshot at [project_files.js](C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2_workers/dev1/desktop/src/project/project_files.js:358). If settings capture the old list while a pin write is pending, their queued save can overwrite the newer list. Updating the open draft after the pin response does not fix the already-sent payload.  
   **Fix:** Make general project-config persistence preserve the current disk `pinnedConversationIds`, since this field is service-owned and not editable. Alternatively, serialize frontend saves behind pending pin writes.

3. **High — External project-config reloads do not update canonical pin state.**  
   File-watcher reload updates only `ConfigService` at [project_loading.ts](C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2_workers/dev1/app/src/services/project/project_loading.ts:864). `ConversationPinService` remains stale. Pins changed through Git pull, branch synchronization, or manual config edits will not update the UI.  
   **Fix:** After reloading project config, reset `ConversationPinService` from the validated `pinnedConversationIds`.

4. **Medium — Popup view data remains component-owned.**  
   [pinned_conversations_indicator.tsx](C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2_workers/dev1/app/src/components/shell/pinned_conversations_indicator.tsx:27) derives card titles, action labels, and availability in React. This violates the rule that services own view data and components only subscribe and render.  
   **Fix:** Expose stable popup items from `AgentIntegration` or a dedicated projection service.

5. **Low — Service subscription starts in a constructor and cannot be cleaned up.**  
   [agent_integration.ts](C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2_workers/dev1/app/src/services/agents/agent_integration.ts:116) subscribes to `ConversationPinService` during construction and discards the cleanup function. This violates the two-phase service lifecycle.  
   **Fix:** Subscribe during `start()`, retain cleanup, and unsubscribe during `reset()` or `stop()`.

6. **Low — Card conversation updates merge the pinned projection twice.**  
   [agent_integration.ts](C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2_workers/dev1/app/src/services/agents/agent_integration.ts:434) calls `upsertAgentConversation()`, which already calls `mergePinnedConversation()`, then calls it again. Pinned updates publish duplicate aggregate events and rerenders.  
   **Fix:** Remove the second call.

7. **Low — Remote pin subscriptions hand-roll a listener registry.**  
   [remote_control_storage_service.ts](C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2_workers/dev1/app/src/services/data/remote_control_storage_service.ts:209) adds listener `Set` and callback `Map` state, contrary to the `EventTarget` rule.  
   **Fix:** Use `EventTarget` for local fan-out and retain only maps required for transport subscription IDs.

Both linters, TypeScript checking, and 216 targeted tests pass. No files were changed.
lets focus first on nr 1, cause I don't understand the problem. you seem to think we need to load the conversations when we load the list of pins?

Not to load pin state. `ConversationPinService` already loads pin IDs from `md2.config.json`.

The problem is resolving those IDs into displayable conversation records. Status popup needs title, `startedAt`, `actionId`, `cardInternalId`, and path. Pin list contains only IDs.

Current flow:

1. Config loads `['conversation-123']`.
2. `AgentIntegration.ensurePinnedConversationsLoaded()` tries to find conversation records.
3. It calls `listAgentConversationReferences()`.
4. Desktop implementation returns only project-origin conversation references.
5. If `conversation-123` belongs to a card, its record is never found after a cold reopen.
6. Pin ID remains correctly stored, but status indicator cannot display it.

Card conversation may appear accidentally if that card’s conversations were loaded elsewhere first. That makes behavior dependent on which cards the user previously opened or hydrated.

We do not necessarily need to load every conversation. Better options are:

- Resolve only pinned IDs through a project-wide ID-to-reference index, if such an index exists.
- Scan current card activity references and stop after all pinned IDs are found.
- Load all current card and project activity records once, which is simplest but potentially heavier.

So the defect is not “pins require conversations.” It is: **the status projection cannot resolve card-owned pin IDs after a cold project load.**

- we should only need to load this at the moment that the list of pins is shown, so when the popup is opened, not when the component is loaded.
- we should not have to load all conversations, just the activity files of the conversations that we have pinned. if this is not possible, than we did not store enough information in the list of pins

Agreed. Current implementation violates both points.

Correct design:

- `PinnedConversationsIndicator` subscribes directly to `ConversationPinService` for visibility and count.
- No conversation records load when the component mounts.
- Clicking the indicator triggers loading of pinned conversation details.
- Only pinned conversations are loaded.

The current `pinnedConversationIds: string[]` is insufficient for targeted loading. A conversation ID does not identify its activity file. Finding it requires scanning activity files.

Store identity plus locator, for example:

```ts
interface PinnedConversationReference {
    conversationId: string;
    conversationPath: string;
}
```

`conversationId` remains canonical identity. `conversationPath` is only the persistence locator used to load the record. This follows the domain rule that paths are references, not identity.

Required changes:

1. Replace `pinnedConversationIds` with validated pinned references.
2. Pass ID and path when pinning.
3. Include the reference in cross-window pin events.
4. Make the indicator count references directly.
5. Remove its mount-time `ensurePinnedConversationsLoaded()` call.
6. Load only referenced conversations when the popup opens.
7. Keep missing or moved persistence targets visible as unavailable entries where possible.

So finding 1 should be restated as: **The stored pin data lacks the persistence reference required for targeted lazy loading, causing the implementation to scan conversations eagerly.**
`conversationPath` no, not allowed, paths can change (release, archive,...). we need another way.
The locator must be stable domain data, not a mutable filesystem path. I’m checking whether activity storage is already derivable from conversation ownership so the pin record can stay minimal.

---

status: ready for implementation
owner: 
affects:

Some conversations remain useful long after they finish. Pinning gives users a project-wide shortlist from which they can identify and reopen those conversations quickly. Pinning affects discoverability only; it does not change conversation lifetime or activity compaction.

## User experience

* A pin/unpin icon appears directly after the conversation picker in the action popup.
* `New conversation` cannot be pinned.
* Pinned entries in the conversation picker show a pin marker. Existing newest-first ordering remains unchanged.
* When the project has pinned conversations, `PinnedConversationsIndicator` appears in the status bar immediately before `RunningAgentsIndicator`.
* Selecting the indicator opens the existing status-details surface. It lists pinned conversations newest first with conversation title, start time, action label, and current card title for card-owned conversations.
* Selecting an available row opens the related action popup with that exact persisted conversation selected.

## Architecture

### Ownership and persistence

`ConversationPinService` is the single owner of pin state for the current project. Its canonical state is an ordered list of `AgentConversation.id` values.

The list is persisted as `pinnedConversations: PinnedConversationLocator[]` in `md2.config.json`. Each locator stores the canonical conversation ID plus `cardInternalId` for card-owned conversations, or the action context kind for conversations without a card. Paths are not stored because release, archive, and other moves can change them. A missing list loads as empty. The service resets from the loaded project configuration whenever the project changes.

`AgentConversation.id` is the pin identity. Conversation paths remain persistence references used to load and open history; they are never used as pin identity.

### Writes and cross-window synchronization

`ConversationPinService.setPinned(locator, pinned)` calls the Electron action bridge. The backend serializes the project-config update, writes the complete updated locator list, and returns that confirmed list. The service publishes state only after the write succeeds, so a failed write leaves the last confirmed snapshot intact.

After persistence, the backend emits `{ locator, pinned }` through `onActionConversationPinned`. Every attached window applies the event to its service-owned list. Aggregate and conversation-scoped `EventTarget` notifications support `useSyncExternalStore` subscriptions without republishing cards or conversation collections.

Project-config drafts receive service-owned list changes as they occur. Saving an already-open settings draft therefore cannot restore an older pin list.

### Pinned conversation projection

`AgentIntegration` owns only the view projection used by the status popup. When that projection is first requested, it loads all current-project activity conversation references, including card- and project-origin conversations, and selects records whose `AgentConversation.id` occurs in `ConversationPinService`.

The projection is sorted by `startedAt`, newest first. Run updates refresh matching projected conversations, while pin-service events add or remove entries. Project changes clear the projection and its loaded candidates before the next project list is resolved.

### UI subscriptions

The picker pin button and picker options subscribe to one conversation ID through `ConversationPinService`. The status indicator subscribes to the aggregate projected list from `AgentIntegration`. Subscriptions live in the smallest component that renders the changing value.

The pin button is disabled while its write is pending. Write and load failures are reported through `dialogService`.

### Opening pinned history

`CardPopupService` opens a pinned conversation by r
[246 characters omitted]
-owned conversations use project context and initialize the same persisted-history selection.
* A renamed or moved card still resolves through `cardInternalId`.
* Missing cards or actions leave the row visible but unavailable. Selecting it reports the reason through `dialogService`.

## Verification

Coverage includes project-config validation and persistence, pin-service state and events, bridge and cross-window synchronization, project reset, pinned projection, picker controls and markers, status indicator behavior, historical opening, missing targets, and write/load failures. Run the affected app and desktop tests and both subproject linters.

## Acceptance criteria

* Selected persisted or live conversation can be pinned and unpinned from icon beside picker; `New conversation` cannot be pinned.
* The project-level pinned identity list survives reload and project reopen.
* Pin changes from another window appear without reloading the project.
* Conversation updates do not change the project pin list.
* Every pinned picker option shows pin marker; unpinned options do not. Existing newest-first order remains unchanged.
* With at least one pinned conversation, status-bar pin appears immediately before running-agents control. With none, pin control is absent.
* Status popup lists every pinned card- and project-origin conversation in current project, newest first, with enough action/card context to distinguish equal titles.
* Selecting available row opens related action popup on exact conversation, including completed historical conversation with no live run.
* Renamed or moved card still opens because ownership resolves through `cardInternalId`, not stored path. Missing card or action leaves row visible and produces clear error instead of opening wrong popup or throwing during render.
* Pin write or load failure leaves last confirmed state intact and is reported through `dialogService`.

- Pins now store `conversationId`, `cardInternalId` when available, and `contextKind` otherwise. No paths are stored.
- Conversations load only after the pinned-conversations button is clicked.
- Loading targets only activity files associated with pinned cards, plus the project activity file for non-card contexts.
- Config, Electron bridge, remote bridge, synchronization, documentation, and affected tests were updated.

design/feature_descriptions/F_349_pin_conversations.md has been implemented incorrectly: instead of saving a boolean on every conversation, we need to store a separate list, at the level of the project, containing the conversation ids that are pinned. so we need to inverse the ownership of who is pinned: it is not the conversation that manages this, but the pin service. so we need to refactor the feature

I’ll trace the current pin persistence, service ownership, UI subscriptions, and tests first. Then I’ll refactor it so project-level pin state is canonical and conversations remain unaware of pinning.

design/feature_descriptions/F_349_pin_conversations.md:18:When there are pinned conversations, put a pin in the status bar. when user clicks on the pin, a popup opens, very similar to the 'running agents' button on the status bar. The popup contains a list of all the pinned conversations. when user clicks on a conversation, the related action popup opens.
design/feature_descriptions/F_349_pin_conversations.md:24:`AgentConversation` has no pinned state. Activity JSON persists conversation data and `viewed`; parser defaults missing `viewed`, while atomic backend updates and cross-window events keep that field synchronized. Conversation picker lists current action/context conversations newest first. `AgentIntegration` loads card conversations by `cardInternalId` and project conversations from activity references, but exposes no project-wide pinned projection. Status bar ends with `RunningAgentsIndicator`; selecting its card run calls `CardPopupService`, which can open live runs but cannot target persisted conversation path.
design/feature_descriptions/F_349_pin_conversations.md:30:* Add required runtime `pinned: boolean` to `AgentConversation`. Persist it in activity conversation JSON; migrate a missing value to `false`. New conversations start unpinned. Parsing and repair reject non-boolean values.
design/feature_descriptions/F_349_pin_conversations.md:31:* Add atomic `updateActionConversationPinned(reference, pinned)` storage and action-bridge APIs, matching viewed-state write serialization. Preserve stored `pinned` during later run checkpoints so stale live data cannot undo a user choice. Publish pinned changes after disk write; local and remote windows apply only that field before emitting a conversation-ID-scoped event.
design/feature_descriptions/F_349_pin_conversations.md:32:* Let `AgentIntegration` own stable project-wide pinned view data. On first pinned-list request, load all current-project activity conversation references, including card- and project-origin records; thereafter merge run updates and pin events by `AgentConversation.id`. Reset data on project switch. Expose it through `EventTarget` and `useSyncExternalStore` without republishing cards.
design/feature_descriptions/F_349_pin_conversations.md:34:* Include `pinned` in picker projection. Append pin icon to each pinned menu option without changing newest-first ordering or selection identity; paths remain persistence references, while `AgentConversation.id` remains conversation identity.
design/feature_descriptions/F_349_pin_conversations.md:35:* Add `PinnedConversationsIndicator` immediately before `RunningAgentsIndicator` in desktop status bar. Hide it when no conversations are pinned. Its button opens existing status-details surface with pinned conversations newest first; each row shows conversation title, start time, action label, and current card title when card-owned.

design/feature_descriptions/F_349_pin_conversations.md:43:* Every pinned picker option shows pin marker; unpinned options do not. Existing newest-first order remains unchanged.

entries.content: The call graph shows the project-level persistence boundary is `md2.config.json`. I’ll use a dedicated conversation pin service as the runtime owner, persist only `pinnedConversationIds` in project config, and keep `AgentConversation` free of pin state. The affected call sites are the picker button/options, the status indicator projection, `AgentIntegration`, the Electron/remote bridge, config parsing/saving, and their focused tests; all should receive the new service-owned behavior. Conversation parsing, activity writes/checkpoints, and ordinary conversation consumers should return to their old pin-agnostic behavior.

expect(() => service.loadProjectConfig({ archivedFolder: 'records', releasesFolder: 'RECORDS' })).toThrow('must not overlap')

        expect(() => service.loadProjectConfig({ diagramsFolder: 'records', releasesFolder: 'records/releases' })).toThrow('must not overlap')
    })

    it('loads and validates diagram output config', () => {
        service.init()
        service.loadProjectConfig({
            diagramFooter: 'Render requested view. Save SVG to {{diagram-file}}.',
            diagramsFolder: 'generated/diagrams',
        })

        expect(service.getProjectConfig()).toMatchObject({
            diagramFooter: 'Render requested view. Save SVG to {{diagram-file}}.',
            diagramsFolder: 'generated/diagrams',
        })
        expect(() => service.loadProjectConfig({ diagramFooter: '' })).toThrow('project.diagramFooter')
        expect(() => service.loadProjectConfig({ diagramFooter: 'Render SVG.' })).toThrow('requires {{diagram-file}} placeholder')
        expect(() => service.loadProjectConfig({ diagramsFolder: '../outside' })).toThrow('must stay inside the project folder')
    })

    it('rejects invalid project config values', () => {
        service.init()

        expect(() => service.loadProjectConfig({ backgroundShade: 'blue', pushMode: 'sometimes' as never })).toThrow('Invalid config value')
        expect(() => service.loadProjectConfig({ backgroundShade: 'blue', states: [{ alwaysVisible: true, state: 'new' }, { alwaysVisible: false, state: 'new' }] })).toThrow('duplicate states')
    })

    it('uses the default background shade when stored project config omits it', () => {
        service.init()

        service.loadProjectConfig({ workingFolder: 'docs' })

        expect(service.getProjectConfig().backgroundShade).toBe('neutral')
    })

    it('rejects unsupported project background shades', () => {
        service.init()

        expect(() => service.loadProjectConfig({ backgroundShade: 'cyan' as never })).toThrow('Invalid config value')
    })

    it('loads project states in their configured order', () => {
        service.init()
        const states = [
            { alwaysVisible: true, color: '#123456', defaultActionId: 'refine', state: 'backlog' },
            { alwaysVisible: false, state: 'shipped' },
        ]

        service.loadProjectConfig({ backgroundShade: 'purple', states })

        expect(service.getProjectConfig().states).toEqual([
            states[0],
            { ...states[1], color: defaultColumnAccent(1) },
        ])
    })

    it('omits absent default action ids from project states', () => {
        service.init()
        service.loadProjectConfig({ states: [{ alwaysVisible: true, state: 'backlog' }] })

        expect(service.getProjectConfig().states[0]).not.toHaveProperty('defaultActionId')
    })

    it.each([null, '', 7])('rejects invalid project state default action id %j', (defaultActionId) => {
        service.init()
        const states = [{ alwaysVisible: true, defaultActionId, state: 'backlog' }]

        expect(() => service.loadProjectConfig({ states } as never)).toThrow('project.states[0].defaultActionId')
    })

    it('keeps active values unchanged when a draft is discarded', () => {
        service.init()
        service.loadProjectConfig(null)
        service.loadDraft()
        service.setDraftValue('project.pushMode', 'auto')
        service.discardDraft()

        expect(service.getProjectConfig().pushMode).toBe('manual')
    })

    it('applies validated draft values on save', () => {
        service.init()
        service.loadProjectConfig(null)
        service.loadDraft()
        service.setDraftValue('project.pushMode', 'auto')
        service.saveDraft()

        expect(service.getProjectConfig().pushMode).toBe('auto')
    })

    it('detects draft changes by config source', () => {
        service.init()
        service.loadProjectConfig(null)

Some conversations remain useful long after they finish. Pinning gives users a project-wide shortlist from which they can identify and reopen those conversations quickly. Pinning affects discoverability only; it does not change conversation lifetime or activity compaction.

## User experience

* A pin/unpin icon appears directly after the conversation picker in the action popup.
* `New conversation` cannot be pinned.
* Pinned entries in the conversation picker show a pin marker. Existing newest-first ordering remains unchanged.
* When the project has pinned conversations, `PinnedConversationsIndicator` appears in the status bar immediately before `RunningAgentsIndicator`.
* Selecting the indicator opens the existing status-details surface. It lists pinned conversations newest first with conversation title, start time, action label, and current card title for card-owned conversations.
* Selecting an available row opens the related action popup with that exact persisted conversation selected.

## Architecture

### Ownership and persistence

`ConversationPinService` is the single owner of pin state for the current project. Its canonical state is an ordered list of `AgentConversation.id` values.

The list is persisted as `pinnedConversationIds: string[]` in `md2.config.json`. A missing list loads as empty. Configuration parsing requires every entry to be a unique, non-empty string. The service resets from the loaded project configuration whenever the project changes.

`AgentConversation.id` is the pin identity. Conversation paths remain persistence references used to load and open history; they are never used as pin identity.

### Writes and cross-window synchronization

`ConversationPinService.setPinned(conversationId, pinned)` calls the Electron action bridge. The backend serializes the project-config update, writes the complete updated ID list, and returns that confirmed list. The service publishes state only after the write succeeds, so a failed write leaves the last confirmed snapshot intact.

After persistence, the backend emits `{ conversationId, pinned }` through `onActionConversationPinned`. Every attached window applies the event to its service-owned list. Aggregate and conversation-scoped `EventTarget` notifications support `useSyncExternalStore` subscriptions without republishing cards or conversation collections.

Project-config drafts receive service-owned list changes as they occur. Saving an already-open settings draft therefore cannot restore an older pin list.

### Pinned conversation projection

`AgentIntegration` owns only the view projection used by the status popup. When that projection is first requested, it loads all current-project activity conversation references, including card- and project-origin conversations, and selects records whose `AgentConversation.id` occurs in `ConversationPinService`.

The projection is sorted by `startedAt`, newest first. Run updates refresh matching projected conversations, while pin-service events add or remove entries. Project changes clear the projection and its loaded candidates before the next project list is resolved.

### UI subscriptions

The picker pin button and picker options subscribe to one conversation ID through `ConversationPinService`. The status indicator subscribes to the aggregate projected list from `AgentIntegration`. Subscriptions live in the smallest component that renders the changing value.

The pin button is disabled while its write is pending. Write and load failures are reported through `dialogService`.

### Opening pinned history

`CardPopupService` opens a pinned conversation by resolving its action and current context:

* Card-owned conversations resolve the card through `cardInternalId`, build context from current card data, select `actionId`, and initialize history selection from the stored conversation path.
* Project-owned conversations use project context and initialize the same persisted-history selection.
* A renamed or moved card still resolves through `cardInternalId`.
* Missing cards or actions leave the row visible but unavailable. Selecting it reports the reason through `dialogService`.

## Verification

Coverage includes project-config validation and persistence, pin-service state and events, bridge and cross-window synchronization, project reset, pinned projection, picker controls and markers, status indicator behavior, historical opening, missing targets, and write/load failures. Run the affected app and desktop tests and both subproject linters.

## acceptance criteria

* Selected persisted or live conversation can be pinned and unpinned from icon beside picker; `New conversation` cannot be pinned.
* The project-level pinned identity list survives reload and project reopen.
* Pin changes from another window appear without reloading the project.
* Conversation updates do not change the project pin list.
* Every pinned picker option shows pin marker; unpinned options do not. Existing newest-first order remains unchanged.
* With at least one pinned conversation, status-bar pin appears immediately before running-agents control. With none, pin control is absent.
* Status popup lists every pinned card- and project-origin conversation in current project, newest first, with enough action/card context to distinguish equal titles.
* Selecting available row opens related action popup on exact conversation, including completed historical conversation with no live run.
* Renamed or moved card still opens because ownership resolves through `cardInternalId`, not stored path. Missing card or action leaves row visible and produces clear error instead of opening wrong popup or throwing during render.
* Pin write or load failure leaves last confirmed state intact and is reported through `dialogService`.

## Current state

`AgentConversation` has no pinned state. ## implementation details

* Add atomic `updateActionConversationPinned(reference, pinned)` storage and action-bridge APIs, matching viewed-state write serialization. Preserve stored `pinned` during later run checkpoints so stale live data cannot undo a user choice. Publish pinned changes after disk write; local and remote windows apply only that field before emitting a conversation-ID-scoped event.
* Let `AgentIntegration` own stable project-wide pinned view data. On first pinned-list request, load all current-project activity conversation references, including card- and project-origin records; thereafter merge run updates and pin events by `AgentConversation.id`. Reset data on project switch. Expose it through `EventTarget` and `useSyncExternalStore` without republishing cards.
* Put pin/unpin icon button directly after agent conversation picker. Disable it for `New conversation`; otherwise reflect displayed live or persisted conversation. Toggle through service, update only after backend success, and report failure through `dialogService`. Include tooltip and `aria-label`.
* Include `pinned` in picker projection. Append pin icon to each pinned menu option without changing newest-first ordering or selection identity; paths remain persistence references, while `AgentConversation.id` remains conversation identity.
* Add `PinnedConversationsIndicator` immediately before `RunningAgentsIndicator` in desktop status bar. Hide it when no conversations are pinned. Its button opens existing status-details surface with pinned conversations newest first; each row shows conversation title, start time, action label, and current card title when card-owned.
* Add persisted-conversation opening to `CardPopupService`: resolve card ownership by `cardInternalId`, build context from current card data, select `actionId`, then initialize history selection from conversation path. Project-origin conversations use project context. If action or card no longer exists, keep row visible but unavailable and report reason through `dialogService` when selected.
* Add parser/persistence, bridge/event, service projection, picker toggle/marker, status indicator, project reset, historical-open, missing-target, and error tests. Run affected app and desktop tests plus each subproject linter.

## acceptance criteria

* Selected persisted or live conversation can be pinned and unpinned from icon beside picker; `New conversation` cannot be pinned.
* Pin state survives reload and project reopen. Later conversation checkpoints and changes from another window do not revert it.
* Every pinned picker option shows pin marker; unpinned options do not. Existing newest-first order remains unchanged.
* With at least one pinned conversation, status-bar pin appears immediately before running-agents control. With none, pin control is absent.
* Status popup lists every pinned card- and project-origin conversation in current project, newest first, with enough action/card context to distinguish equal titles.
* Selecting available row opens related action popup on exact conversation, including completed historical conversation with no live run.
* Renamed or moved card still opens because ownership resolves through `cardInternalId`, not stored path. Missing card or action leaves row visible and produces clear error instead of opening wrong popup or throwing during render.
* Pin write or load failure leaves last confirmed state intact and is reported through `dialogService`.

---

# Architectural decisions

Project-wide decisions for MDÂ². The app is a Vite React web app in `app/`; `desktop/` is a separate Electron host that can load the website and expose local capabilities through preload bridges.

## File naming

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Code files use lowercase snake_case names. | All code files in `app/src/` and `desktop/` use lowercase words separated by underscores, for example `github_auth_service.ts`, `project_workspace.tsx`, and `local_git_service.js`. Test files keep the same base name with `.test` before the extension, for example `github_auth_service.test.ts`. Exported symbols keep normal TypeScript/JavaScript casing such as `GithubAuthService`, `ProjectWorkspace`, and `useGithubAuth`. | A single file naming convention avoids mixed PascalCase, camelCase, and hyphenated filenames, and keeps imports predictable across Windows and case-sensitive environments. |

## Services and state

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Global singleton services own domain state and logic. | Each domain is a class in `src/services/**`, instantiated once at module level and exported, for example `export const indexesService = new IndexesService()`. React components do not own domain state. | Keeps business logic out of components, testable without a DOM, and shared across windows/views without Redux, Zustand, or Context stores. |
| Service location follows usage scope. | If a service is specific to one UI element and used only there, place it beside that component. Generic or shared services, such as logging, database access, config, storage, or cross-screen domain logic, belong in `src/services/`. | Keeps component-owned behavior local while preserving `src/services/` for reusable application services. |
| Consumers use direct imports or the service injector. | Direct import when no import cycle exists; use `src/services/service_injector.js` when a cycle would occur. Every global singleton service registers itself in its constructor with `inj.register('myService', this)`. | The service graph is dense; the injector is a bare global registry that defers resolution to call time. |
| Services have a two-phase lifecycle. | Constructors only register and set unloaded state such as `null`. Config-dependent or service-dependent work runs in `init()`, `start()`, app bootstrap (`App.jsx`), or a `loaded` lifecycle event. `configService.config` is private; callers use `get`, `set`, and `clear`. | Module evaluation order is not guaranteed, so `configService` is not usable at import time. Reading config in a constructor is a bug. |

## Card state

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The application has one `Card` domain type. | Do not create separate canonical, project, snapshot, or editor card types. The card-owning service holds the loaded cards and exposes focused operations that change only the requested field. React snapshots and editor drafts are read values; they must never replace or merge a complete card. Parser bookkeeping may remain private persistence metadata, but it is not another card model. | One card concept gives state a clear owner and prevents stale copies from overwriting newer worktree, activity, ordering, policy, or body values. |
| Card UI subscribes at field level. | A component subscribes only to the primitive or stable reference it renders, using granular `EventTarget` events and `useSyncExternalStore`. Do not clone or stringify a complete card to detect a field change. Group fields only in a deliberately small, stable projection when they are always rendered together. | A one-field change allocates and rerenders only what consumes that field, keeping memory use bounded and the UI responsive. |
| Cards are serialized only at persistence boundaries. | Mutate the owned `Card` through a focused operation, then serialize its current state when the persistence batch flushes. Editor changes update only the edited field. Activity linking updates only activity references. External file changes are parsed and applied deliberately without replacing dirty local state. | Persistence remains deterministic while concurrent saves and external updates cannot discard unrelated newer values. |


## Events and React integration

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Services notify observers through their own `EventTarget`. | Services expose an `EventTarget` and dispatch named `CustomEvent` domain events such as `activeIndex`, `added`, `deleted`, or `changedBox`. Observers subscribe with `addEventListener` and unsubscribe with `removeEventListener` on the owning service. | Decouples producers from consumers without depending on Node `EventEmitter`, which is not available in the browser-first React app. |
| Custom hooks bridge service events to functional components. | Hooks in `src/components/hooks/`, such as `useActiveIndex` and `useProjectConfig`, seed `useState` from a service property, subscribe in `useEffect`, unsubscribe in cleanup, and return the value. Prefer hook + service over prop chains. | Components stay declarative and avoid direct event plumbing. |
| Components subscribe at the smallest rendering boundary. | Root and layout components compose UI regions and pass structural inputs. Components that render changing application data subscribe through hooks themselves. Do not hoist changing data into ancestors only to pass it downward. | Limits rerenders to affected UI, protects transient state such as open popups, and avoids broad prop chains. |
| Components use the app theme service path. | `App` owns theme mode through `useThemeMode()`, builds the MUI theme with `createAppTheme(mode)`, and provides it through `ThemeProvider`. Components read theme values with MUI APIs such as `useTheme`, `useMediaQuery`, and `sx`; only controls that change the palette mode receive `mode` and `onToggleTheme`. | Theme state, persistence, and palette construction stay centralized while components remain presentation-focused. |

import type { ActionFile } from './action_types'
import type { AnySchedule } from './action_schedule_types'

    DEFAULT_WORKING_FOLDER,
}
export const DEFAULT_DIFF_COMMAND = 'git show {{commit}}'
export const AUTO_COMMIT_DELAY_MS = 30000

/** Card type id; projects can configure custom types beyond the default feature/job/bug. */
export type CardType = string
export type PushMode = 'auto' | 'manual'

export interface CardTypeConfig {
    color: string
    idPrefix: string
    label: string
    type: CardType
}

export interface StateConfig {
    alwaysVisible: boolean
    color?: string
    defaultActionId?: string
    state: string
}

export interface ProjectConfig {
    actionsFolder: string
    archivedFolder: string
    backgroundShade: ProjectBackgroundShade
    cardSeparator: CardSeparator
    cardTypes: CardTypeConfig[]
    diffCommand: string
    diagramFooter: string
    diagramsFolder: string
    projectFolder: string
    pushMode: PushMode
    releasesFolder: string
    states: StateConfig[]
    workingFolder: string
}

/** How a file's `content` is encoded for the storage write path. Binary assets use base64. */
export type FileEncoding = 'utf-8' | 'base64'

export interface MarkdownFile {
    content: string
    encoding?: FileEncoding
    path: string
    sha?: string
}

export interface ProjectAsset {
    content: string
    contentType: string
    encoding: 'base64'
    path: string
}

export interface CardHeader {
    affects: string[]
    after: string | null
    /** Terminal conversation references inside activity files; the name mirrors the persisted `agents` field. */
    agentLogReferences: string[]
    author: string | null
    branch?: string | null
    changedFiles: string[]
    id: string
    internalId: string | null
    owner: string | null
    policy: Record<string, boolean>
    references: string[]
    sentryBaseUrl?: string
    sentryIssueId?: string
    sentryOrganization?: string
    status: string | null
    title: string
    worktree?: number | null
    worktreeError?: string | null
    worktreeValue?: string | null
}

export interface Card {
    agentConversationErrors: AgentConversationError[]
    agentConversations: AgentConversation[]
    content: string
    hasFrontmatter: boolean
    header: CardHeader
    isActive: boolean
    path: string
    sha?: string
}

export interface ProjectSnapshot {
    activeCards: Card[]
    backgroundCards: Card[]
    repositoryFiles: string[]
    workingFolder: string
}

export interface CardDraft {
    body: string
    title: string
    type: CardType
}

export interface ProjectReference {
    branch: string
    id: string
    owner?: string
    repository?: string
    rootPath?: string
}

/** The disposition of the checkout folder when a linked worktree is removed from Git. */
export type WorktreeRemovalMode = 'files' | 'folder' | 'unregister'

    error: string | null

    parkingBranch: string | null
    path: string
    status: WorktreeStat

const BUG_CARD_COLOR = '#d32f2f'

export const DEFAULT_COLUMN_ACCENTS = ['#9c4dcc', '#29a8e0', '#ed6c02', '#f9a825', '#43a047']

/** Resolve the repeating default accent assigned by configured column position. */
export function defaultColumnAccent(index: number) {
    if (!Number.isInteger(index) || index < 0) throw new Error(`Invalid column index: ${index}`)

    return DEFAULT_COLUMN_ACCENTS[index % DEFAULT_COLUMN_ACCENTS.length]
}

export const DEFAULT_CARD_TYPES: CardTypeConfig[] = [
    { color: DEFAULT_COLOR_SCHEME.primary.regular, idPrefix: 'F', label: 'Feature', type: 'feature' },
    { color: DEFAULT_COLOR_SCHEME.secondary.regular, idPrefix: 'J', label: 'Job', type: 'job' },
    { color: BUG_CARD_COLOR, idPrefix: 'B', label: 'Bug', type: 'bug' },
]

export const DEFAULT_STATES: StateConfig[] = [
    { alwaysVisible: true, color: defaultColumnAccent(0), state: 'new' },
    { alwaysVisible: true, color: defaultColumnAccent(1), state: 'design' },
    { alwaysVisible: true, color: defaultColumnAccent(2), state: 'ready for implementation' },
    { alwaysVisible: true, color: defaultColumnAccent(3), state: 'to fix' },
    { alwaysVisible: true, color: defaultColumnAccent(4), state: 'ready' },
]

export function resolveProjectConfigPaths(config: ProjectConfig): ProjectConfig {
    return {
        ...config,
        actionsFolder: joinProjectFolderPath(config.projectFolder, config.actionsFolder),
        archivedFolder: joinProjectFolderPath(config.projectFolder, config.archivedFolder),
        diagramsFolder: joinProjectFolderPath(config.projectFolder, config.diagramsFolder),
        releasesFolder: joinProjectFolderPath(config.projectFolder, config.releasesFolder),
        workingFolder: joinProjectFolderPath(config.projectFolder, config.workingFolder),
    }
}

    actionsFolder: DEFAULT_ACTIONS_FOLDER,
    archivedFolder: DEFAULT_ARCHIVED_FOLDER,
    backgroundShade: 'neutral',
    cardSeparator: DEFAULT_CARD_SEPARATOR,
    cardTypes: DEFAULT_CARD_TYPES,
    diffCommand: DEFAULT_DIFF_COMMAND,
    diagramFooter: DEFAULT_DIAGRAM_FOOTER,
    diagramsFolder: DEFAULT_DIAGRAMS_FOLDER,
    projectFolder: DEFAULT_PROJECT_FOLDER,
    pushMode: 'manual',
    releasesFolder: DEFAULT_RELEASES_FOLDER,
    states: DEFAULT_STATES,
    workingFolder: DEFAULT_WORKING_FOLDER,
}

import { Box, MenuItem } from '@mui/material'
import type { MenuItemProps } from '@mui/material'
import PushPinOutlined from '@mui/icons-material/PushPinOutlined'
import { useConversationPinned } from '../../hooks/use_conversation_pinned'
import { conversationPickerLabel, type ConversationPickerConversation } from './action_conversation_picker_data'

interface ActionConversationPickerOptionProps extends Omit<MenuItemProps, 'value'> {
    conversation: ConversationPickerConversation
    value: string
}

/** Renders one history option with live confirmed pin state. */
export function ActionConversationPickerOption({ conversation, ...menuItemProps }: ActionConversationPickerOptionProps) {
    const pinned = useConversationPinned(conversation)

    return (
        <MenuItem {...menuItemProps}>
            <Box component="span" sx={{ flex: 1, minWidth: 0 }}>{conversationPickerLabel(conversation)}</Box>
            {pinned && <PushPinOutlined aria-label="Pinned" sx={{ fontSize: 15, ml: 1 }} />}
        </MenuItem>

The feature is not fully correct. Five problems found.

1. **Critical — Card-owned pinned conversations are not loaded project-wide.**  
   [AgentIntegration](C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2_workers/dev1/app/src/services/agents/agent_integration.ts:435) assumes `listAgentConversationReferences()` returns card and project conversations. The desktop implementation only reads the project activity file at [activity_files.js](C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2_workers/dev1/desktop/src/actions/activity/activity_files.js:484). Most card pins will therefore be absent from the status bar until separately loaded elsewhere.  
   **Fix:** Combine project conversation references with every current card’s `agentLogReferences`, deduplicate them, and load all conversations from those activity files.

2. **High — Remote pinning of an unloaded conversation is ignored.**  
   Initial loading discards every unpinned conversation at [agent_integration.ts](C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2_workers/dev1/app/src/services/agents/agent_integration.ts:444). Later pin events contain only conversation ID and boolean. `applyConversationPinned()` cannot add a conversation it no longer knows at [agent_integration.ts](C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2_workers/dev1/app/src/services/agents/agent_integration.ts:302). The remote window remains stale indefinitely.  
   **Fix:** Retain a project-wide conversation map keyed by `AgentConversation.id`, then derive the pinned array from it. Merge pin events into that map.

3. **High — Pin button can perform the opposite stale action after a remote update.**  
   The icon reads confirmed state through `useConversationPinned`, but the command negates the stale conversation prop at [action_conversation_store.ts](C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2_workers/dev1/app/src/components/actions/conversation/action_conversation_store.ts:209). After another window changes the pin, clicking “Unpin” may send `true` again, or “Pin” may send `false`.  
   **Fix:** Pass the hook’s current confirmed value into the toggle callback and persist its explicit inverse.

4. **Medium — View data is owned by the React component.**  
   [pinned_conversations_indicator.tsx](C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2_workers/dev1/app/src/components/shell/pinned_conversations_indicator.tsx:27) resolves action labels, card titles, and availability inside React. This violates the project rule that services own model and view data while components subscribe and render.  
   **Fix:** Move the stable `PinnedConversationDetailsItem` projection into `AgentIntegration` or a dedicated service. Publish scoped `EventTarget` updates.

5. **Low — New remote subscription code hand-rolls a listener registry.**  
   [remote_control_storage_service.ts](C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2_workers/dev1/app/src/services/data/remote_control_storage_service.ts:209) adds listener `Set` and callback `Map` collections. Project rules explicitly prohibit custom listener registries.  
   **Fix:** Use `EventTarget` for local listeners. Keep only transport request/subscription-ID maps required for remote protocol routing.

App lint, desktop lint, TypeScript checking, and 208 targeted tests pass. Existing tests mock a broader reference-listing contract than desktop provides, masking problem 1. No files were changed.

Some conversations remain useful long after they finish. Pinning gives users a project-wide shortlist from which they can identify and reopen those conversations quickly. Pinning affects discoverability only; it does not change conversation lifetime or activity compaction.

## User experience

* A pin/unpin icon appears directly after the conversation picker in the action popup.
* `New conversation` cannot be pinned.
* Pinned entries in the conversation picker show a pin marker. Existing newest-first ordering remains unchanged.
* When the project has pinned conversations, `PinnedConversationsIndicator` appears in the status bar immediately before `RunningAgentsIndicator`.
* Selecting the indicator opens the existing status-details surface. It lists pinned conversations newest first with conversation title, start time, action label, and current card title for card-owned conversations.
* Selecting an available row opens the related action popup with that exact persisted conversation selected.

## Architecture

### Ownership and persistence

`ConversationPinService` is the single owner of pin state for the current project. Its canonical state is an ordered list of `AgentConversation.id` values.

The list is persisted as `pinnedConversationIds: string[]` in `md2.config.json`. A missing list loads as empty. Configuration parsing requires every entry to be a unique, non-empty string. The service resets from the loaded project configuration whenever the project changes.

`AgentConversation.id` is the pin identity. Conversation paths remain persistence references used to load and open history; they are never used as pin identity.

### Writes and cross-window synchronization

`ConversationPinService.setPinned(conversationId, pinned)` calls the Electron action bridge. The backend serializes the project-config update, writes the complete updated ID list, and returns that confirmed list. The service publishes state only after the write succeeds, so a failed write leaves the last confirmed snapshot intact.

After persistence, the backend emits `{ conversationId, pinned }` through `onActionConversationPinned`. Every attached window applies the event to its service-owned list. Aggregate and conversation-scoped `EventTarget` notifications support `useSyncExternalStore` subscriptions without republishing cards or conversation collections.

Project-config drafts receive service-owned list changes as they occur. Saving an already-open settings draft therefore cannot restore an older pin list.

### Pinned conversation projection

`AgentIntegration` owns only the view projection used by the status popup. When that projection is first requested, it loads all current-project activity conversation references, including card- and project-origin conversations, and selects records whose `AgentConversation.id` occurs in `ConversationPinService`.

The projection is sorted by `startedAt`, newest first. Run updates refresh matching projected conversations, while pin-service events add or remove entries. Project changes clear the projection and its loaded candidates before the next project list is resolved.

### UI subscriptions

The picker pin button and picker options subscribe to one conversation ID through `ConversationPinService`. The status indicator subscribes to the aggregate projected list from `AgentIntegration`. Subscriptions live in the smallest component that renders the changing value.

The pin button is disabled while its write is pending. Write and load failures are reported through `dialogService`.

### Opening pinned history

`CardPopupService` opens a pinned conversation by resolving its action and current context:

* Card-owned conversations resolve the card through `cardInternalId`, build context from current card data, select `actionId`, and initialize history selection from the stored conversation path.
* Project-owned conversations use project context and initialize the same persisted-history selection.
* A renamed or moved card still resolves through `cardInternalId`.
* Missing cards or actions leave the row visible but unavailable. Selecting it reports the reason through `dialogService`.

## Verification

Coverage includes project-config validation and persistence, pin-service state and events, bridge and cross-window synchronization, project reset, pinned projection, picker controls and markers, status indicator behavior, historical opening, missing targets, and write/load failures. Run the affected app and desktop tests and both subproject linters.

## Acceptance criteria

* Selected persisted or live conversation can be pinned and unpinned from icon beside picker; `New conversation` cannot be pinned.
* The project-level pinned identity list survives reload and project reopen.
* Pin changes from another window appear without reloading the project.
* Conversation updates do not change the project pin list.
* Every pinned picker option shows pin marker; unpinned options do not. Existing newest-first order remains unchanged.
* With at least one pinned conversation, status-bar pin appears immediately before running-agents control. With none, pin control is absent.
* Status popup lists every pinned card- and project-origin conversation in current project, newest first, with enough action/card context to distinguish equal titles.
* Selecting available row opens related action popup on exact conversation, including completed historical conversation with no live run.
* Renamed or moved card still opens because ownership resolves through `cardInternalId`, not stored path. Missing card or action leaves row visible and produces clear error instead of opening wrong popup or throwing during render.
* Pin write or load failure leaves last confirmed state intact and is reported through `dialogService`.

# Architectural decisions

Project-wide decisions for MDÂ². The app is a Vite React web app in `app/`; `desktop/` is a separate Electron host that can load the website and expose local capabilities through preload bridges.

## File naming

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Code files use lowercase snake_case names. | All code files in `app/src/` and `desktop/` use lowercase words separated by underscores, for example `github_auth_service.ts`, `project_workspace.tsx`, and `local_git_service.js`. Test files keep the same base name with `.test` before the extension, for example `github_auth_service.test.ts`. Exported symbols keep normal TypeScript/JavaScript casing such as `GithubAuthService`, `ProjectWorkspace`, and `useGithubAuth`. | A single file naming convention avoids mixed PascalCase, camelCase, and hyphenated filenames, and keeps imports predictable across Windows and case-sensitive environments. |

## Services and state

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Global singleton services own domain state and logic. | Each domain is a class in `src/services/**`, instantiated once at module level and exported, for example `export const indexesService = new IndexesService()`. React components do not own domain state. | Keeps business logic out of components, testable without a DOM, and shared across windows/views without Redux, Zustand, or Context stores. |
| Service location follows usage scope. | If a service is specific to one UI element and used only there, place it beside that component. Generic or shared services, such as logging, database access, config, storage, or cross-screen domain logic, belong in `src/services/`. | Keeps component-owned behavior local while preserving `src/services/` for reusable application services. |
| Consumers use direct imports or the service injector. | Direct import when no import cycle exists; use `src/services/service_injector.js` when a cycle would occur. Every global singleton service registers itself in its constructor with `inj.register('myService', this)`. | The service graph is dense; the injector is a bare global registry that defers resolution to call time. |
| Services have a two-phase lifecycle. | Constructors only register and set unloaded state such as `null`. Config-dependent or service-dependent work runs in `init()`, `start()`, app bootstrap (`App.jsx`), or a `loaded` lifecycle event. `configService.config` is private; callers use `get`, `set`, and `clear`. | Module evaluation order is not guaranteed, so `configService` is not usable at import time. Reading config in a constructor is a bug. |

## Card state

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The application has one `Card` domain type. | Do not create separate canonical, project, snapshot, or editor card types. The card-owning service holds the loaded cards and exposes focused operations that change only the requested field. React snapshots and editor drafts are read values; they must never replace or merge a complete card. Parser bookkeeping may remain private persistence metadata, but it is not another card model. | One card concept gives state a clear owner and prevents stale copies from overwriting newer worktree, activity, ordering, policy, or body values. |
| Card UI subscribes at field level. | A component subscribes only to the primitive or stable reference it renders, using granular `EventTarget` events and `useSyncExternalStore`. Do not clone or stringify a complete card to detect a field change. Group fields only in a deliberately small, stable projection when they are always rendered together. | A one-field change allocates and rerenders only what consumes that field, keeping memory use bounded and the UI responsive. |
| Cards are serialized only at persistence boundaries. | Mutate the owned `Card` through a focused operation, then serialize its current state when the persistence batch flushes. Editor changes update only the edited field. Activity linking updates only activity references. External file changes are parsed and applied deliberately without replacing dirty local state. | Persistence remains deterministic while concurrent saves and external updates cannot discard unrelated newer values. |


## Events and React integration

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Services notify observers through their own `EventTarget`. | Services expose an `EventTarget` and dispatch named `CustomEvent` domain events such as `activeIndex`, `added`, `deleted`, or `changedBox`. Observers subscribe with `addEventListener` and unsubscribe with `removeEventListener` on the owning service. | Decouples producers from consumers without depending on Node `EventEmitter`, which is not available in the browser-first React app. |
| Custom hooks bridge service events to functional components. | Hooks in `src/components/hooks/`, such as `useActiveIndex` and `useProjectConfig`, seed `useState` from a service property, subscribe in `useEffect`, unsubscribe in cleanup, and return the value. Prefer hook + service over prop chains. | Components stay declarative and avoid direct event plumbing. |
| Components subscribe at the smallest rendering boundary. | Root and layout components compose UI regions and pass structural inputs. Components that render changing application data subscribe through hooks themselves. Do not hoist changing data into ancestors only to pass it downward. | Limits rerenders to affected UI, protects transient state such as open popups, and avoids broad prop chains. |
| Components use the app theme service path. | `App` owns theme mode through `useThemeMode()`, builds the MUI theme with `createAppTheme(mode)`, and provides it through `ThemeProvider`. Components read theme values with MUI APIs such as `useTheme`, `useMediaQuery`, and `sx`; only controls that change the palette mode receive `mode` and `onToggleTheme`. | Theme state, persistence, and palette construction stay centralized while components remain presentation-focused. |

    (entry) => entry.source === 'react',
).map((entry) => entry.key)

export function createDefaultValues(): ConfigValues {
    return CONFIG_ENTRIES.reduce((values, entry) => ({ ...values, [entry.key]: entry.defaultValue }), {} as ConfigValues)
}

    const entry = CONFIG_ENTRY_BY_KEY.get(key)
    if (!entry) throw new Error(`Unknown config key: ${key}`)

The new pin-state architecture is implemented, and conversations no longer contain `pinned`. Seven problems remain.

1. **Critical — Card conversations are still missing from project-wide loading.**  
   [AgentIntegration](C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2_workers/dev1/app/src/services/agents/agent_integration.ts:379) expects `listAgentConversationReferences()` to include card conversations. Its desktop implementation only reads project activity at [activity_files.js](C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2_workers/dev1/desktop/src/actions/activity/activity_files.js:484). The status popup will miss most card-owned pins.  
   **Fix:** Combine project references with every current card’s `agentLogReferences`, loading card activity through `loadActivityConversations()`. The current test incorrectly mocks the reference API as returning both kinds.

2. **High — Concurrent settings save can overwrite a confirmed pin change.**  
   Pin updates read and merge the latest disk config at [project_files.js](C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2_workers/dev1/desktop/src/project/project_files.js:373). Normal config saving writes the complete renderer snapshot at [project_files.js](C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2_workers/dev1/desktop/src/project/project_files.js:358). If settings capture the old list while a pin write is pending, their queued save can overwrite the newer list. Updating the open draft after the pin response does not fix the already-sent payload.  
   **Fix:** Make general project-config persistence preserve the current disk `pinnedConversationIds`, since this field is service-owned and not editable. Alternatively, serialize frontend saves behind pending pin writes.

3. **High — External project-config reloads do not update canonical pin state.**  
   File-watcher reload updates only `ConfigService` at [project_loading.ts](C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2_workers/dev1/app/src/services/project/project_loading.ts:864). `ConversationPinService` remains stale. Pins changed through Git pull, branch synchronization, or manual config edits will not update the UI.  
   **Fix:** After reloading project config, reset `ConversationPinService` from the validated `pinnedConversationIds`.

4. **Medium — Popup view data remains component-owned.**  
   [pinned_conversations_indicator.tsx](C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2_workers/dev1/app/src/components/shell/pinned_conversations_indicator.tsx:27) derives card titles, action labels, and availability in React. This violates the rule that services own view data and components only subscribe and render.  
   **Fix:** Expose stable popup items from `AgentIntegration` or a dedicated projection service.

5. **Low — Service subscription starts in a constructor and cannot be cleaned up.**  
   [agent_integration.ts](C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2_workers/dev1/app/src/services/agents/agent_integration.ts:116) subscribes to `ConversationPinService` during construction and discards the cleanup function. This violates the two-phase service lifecycle.  
   **Fix:** Subscribe during `start()`, retain cleanup, and unsubscribe during `reset()` or `stop()`.

6. **Low — Card conversation updates merge the pinned projection twice.**  
   [agent_integration.ts](C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2_workers/dev1/app/src/services/agents/agent_integration.ts:434) calls `upsertAgentConversation()`, which already calls `mergePinnedConversation()`, then calls it again. Pinned updates publish duplicate aggregate events and rerenders.  
   **Fix:** Remove the second call.

7. **Low — Remote pin subscriptions hand-roll a listener registry.**  
   [remote_control_storage_service.ts](C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2_workers/dev1/app/src/services/data/remote_control_storage_service.ts:209) adds listener `Set` and callback `Map` state, contrary to the `EventTarget` rule.  
   **Fix:** Use `EventTarget` for local fan-out and retain only maps required for transport subscription IDs.

    cancelled: 'cancelled',

    failed: 'failed',
    okButNotAfter: 'completed',

const MAX_REPORTED_LOAD_ERROR_KEYS = 200
const PINNED_CONVERSATIONS_CHANGED_EVENT = 'pinned-conversations'

function conversationTimestamp(conversation: AgentConversation) {
    const timestamp = Date.parse(conversation.startedAt)

    return Number.isNaN(timestamp) ? 0 : timestamp
}

function sortPinnedConversations(conversations: AgentConversation[]) {
    return conversations.sort((left, right) => conversationTimestamp(right) - conversationTimestamp(left))
}

interface ResolvedAgentConversations {
    conversations: AgentConversation[]
    errors: AgentConversationError[]
    /** Activity files that loaded without failing, so an empty card is distinguishable from a failed one. */
    loadedActivityCount: number
}

export interface AgentIntegrationDeps {
    conversationsChanged(cardPath: string): void
    findCardByInternalId(cardInternalId: string): Card | null
    isCurrentLoad(project: ProjectReference, projectLoadToken: number): boolean
    pins: ConversationPinService
    project(): ProjectReference | null
    requireDependencies(): RequiredDataServiceDependencies
    snapshot(): ProjectSnapshot | null
}

function isOnStateActionError(error: AgentConversationError) {
    return error.kind === 'onStateAction'
}

async function resolveCardConversations(
    card: Card,
    project: ProjectReference,
    storage: StorageService,
): Promise<ResolvedAgentConversations> {
    const activityPaths = [...new Set(card.header.agentLogReferences)]
    const results = await mapWithConcurrency(activityPaths, AGENT_CONVERSATION_LOAD_CONCURRENCY, async (activityPath) => {
        try {
            const conversations = await loadActivityConversations(storage, project, activityPath)

            return { conversations, error: null }
        } catch (error) {
            telemetryService.captureError(error)
            const message = error instanceof Error ? error.message : 'Agent conversation failed to load'

            return { conversations: null, error: { message, path: activityPath } }
        }
    })

    return {
        conversations: results.flatMap(({ conversations }) => conversations ?? []),
        errors: results.flatMap(({ error }) => error ? [error] : []),
        loadedActivityCount: results.filter(({ error }) => !error).length,
    }
}

e project-config update, writes the complete updated locator list, and returns that confirmed list. The service publishes state only after the write succeeds, so a failed write leaves the last confirmed snapshot intact.

After persistence, the backend emits `{ locator, pinned }` through `onActionConversationPinned`. Every attached window applies the event to its service-owned list. Aggregate and conversation-scoped `EventTarget` notifications support `useSyncExternalStore` subscriptions without republishing cards or conversation collections.

Project-config drafts receive service-owned list changes as they occur. Saving an already-open settings draft therefore cannot restore an older pin list.

### Pinned conversation projection

`AgentIntegration` owns only the view projection used by the status popup. Opening the popup requests that projection. It resolves each locator through the current card's activity references or the project activity path, loads only those distinct activity files, and selects records whose `AgentConversation.id` occurs in `ConversationPinService`.

The projection is sorted by `startedAt`, newest first. Run updates refresh matching projected conversations, while pin-service events add or remove entries. Project changes clear the projection and its loaded candidates before the next project list is resolved.

### UI subscriptions

The picker pin button and picker options subscribe to one conversation ID through `ConversationPinService`. The status indicator subscribes to the locator list for visibility and count, and the open popup subscribes to the projected records from `AgentIntegration`. Subscriptions live in the smallest component that renders the changing value.

The pin button is disabled while its write is pending. Write and load failures are reported through `dialogService`.

### Opening pinned history

`CardPopupService` opens a pinned conversation by resolving its action and current context:

* Card-owned conversations resolve the card through `cardInternalId`, build context from current card data, select `actionId`, and initialize history selection from the stored conversation path.
* Project-owned conversations use project context and initialize the same persisted-history selection.
* A renamed or moved card still resolves through `cardInternalId`.
* Missing cards or actions leave the row visible but unavailable. Selecting it reports the reason through `dialogService`.

## Verification

Coverage includes project-config validation and persistence, pin-service state and events, bridge and cross-window synchronization, project reset, pinned projection, picker controls and markers, status indicator behavior, historical opening, missing targets, and write/load failures. Run the affected app and desktop tests and both subproject linters.

## Acceptance criteria

* Selected persisted or live conversation can be pinned and unpinned from icon beside picker; `New conversation` cannot be pinned.
* The project-level pinned identity list survives reload and project reopen.
* Pin changes from another window appear without reloading the project.
* Conversation updates do not change the project pin list.
* Every pinned picker option shows pin marker; unpinned options do not. Existing newest-first order remains unchanged.
* With at least one pinned conversation, status-bar pin appears immediately before running-agents control. With none, pin control is absent.
* Status popup lists every pinned card- and project-origin conversation in current project, newest first, with enough action/card context to distinguish equal titles.
* Selecting available row opens related action popup on exact conversation, including completed historical conversation with no live run.
* Renamed or moved card still opens because ownership resolves through `cardInternalId`, not stored path. Missing card or action leaves row visible and produces clear error instead of opening wrong popup or throwing during render.
* Pin write or load failure leaves last confirmed state intact and is reported through `dialogService`.

Problem 2 is real, but writes are serialized. Problem is stale snapshots, not simultaneous file writes.

Config exists in three places:

- `ConfigService.values` and `draftValues` in [config_service.ts](C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2_workers/dev1/app/src/services/config/config_service.ts:367).
- Pin state in `ConversationPinService`.
- Persisted `md2.config.json`.

Two independent write paths target same file:

1. Settings sends complete `ConfigService` snapshot through [project_loading.ts](C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2_workers/dev1/app/src/services/project/project_loading.ts:284).
2. Pinning calls `updateProjectConversationPinned()`, which reloads disk config, changes pins, then writes complete config in [project_files.js](C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2_workers/dev1/desktop/src/project/project_files.js:387).

`withGitIndexMutation()` serializes both operations, but does not merge snapshots.

Failure sequence:

1. Settings captures config containing old pins.
2. Pin update enters queue and writes new pins.
3. Settings save enters afterward and writes its already-captured full config.
4. New pins are lost.

This can happen between two windows, or within one window when pin write is pending while settings save starts. `SaveStateService` only tracks operations; it does not block or serialize callers.

Other full-config writers exist during project creation and missing-config initialization, but they do not normally overlap an opened project’s pin operations.

Fix: create one backend `ProjectConfigService` as sole config writer. Settings must submit field changes, not a full renderer snapshot. Pinning must submit a pin mutation. Service serializes mutations against its latest canonical config and writes resulting config once.

Agreed. My previous framing overemphasized `draftValues`.

Actual problem is split ownership:

- `ConversationPinService.setPinned()` bypasses `ConfigService` and calls Electron directly.
- Desktop independently reads and writes `md2.config.json`.
- `ConfigService.setPinnedConversations()` only mirrors the completed write afterward.
- Config reload updates `ConfigService`, but `ConversationPinService` does not subscribe to it.

Fix:

- `ConversationPinService` reads and writes pin state only through `ConfigService`.
- `ConfigService` becomes sole owner of config persistence and write serialization.
- `ConversationPinService` subscribes to `ConfigService` changes and refreshes its snapshot after load/reload.
- Remove `updateProjectConversationPinned()` as an independent config writer.
- Keep drafts limited to dialog lifetime. If config changes while dialog is open, canonical non-editable values must remain authoritative when saving.

This also absorbs previous problem 3; config reload synchronization is part of the same ownership defect.

now lets look at 4: I think your analysis is wrong: the data you are describing should not remain in memory, it is loaded at the moment that the popup opens, and should be unloaded again after close, so the behaviour is correct. this is view-data, not model data

My original problem 4 is wrong. Transient popup labels, card titles, and availability are view data and may be derived by the popup component.

However, current implementation does not unload conversations when popup closes:

- `handleClose()` only clears `anchorElement`.
- `AgentIntegration` retains `pinnedConversations`, candidates, and completed-load state until project reset.
- Later pin changes can trigger background loading while popup is closed.

So remove original issue 4, but add a narrower issue:

**Pinned popup data remains loaded after close.**

Fix: expose a cleanup operation that clears the pinned projection, candidates, and load flags, then call it from `handleClose()`.
`Later pin changes can trigger background loading while popup is closed.` this is the only thing I see as a problem. what is loaded in the background whine popup is closed?

After popup has been opened once, `pinnedLoadRequested` remains `true`.

When a new pin cannot be resolved from existing memory, `handlePinsChanged()` calls `ensurePinnedConversationsLoaded()` even while popup is closed. That loads:

- Every distinct activity file referenced by all current pinned locators.
- Every conversation contained in those activity files.
- Matching pinned conversations are then selected; other loaded conversations remain as candidates.

Unpinning does not normally trigger this. Pinning an already-known conversation also avoids loading.

Fix: clear `pinnedLoadRequested` when popup closes, or track popup-open state explicitly and only resolve new pins while open.
if pinnedLoadRequested is not needed, use the popup open state
fix it

I’ll replace the “ever requested” flag with explicit popup-open state. New unresolved pins will reload activity files only while the popup is open; closing or losing the last pin will disable background resolution.
